story.head: A long night for the Kraken’s goalie
paras: The Ducks (11-11-1) lost 4-0 to Colorado on Thursday, while the Kraken (10-8-1) beat Vancouver 5-1 the same night. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Ducks third (19th in the NHL) and the Kraken fifth (tied for 23rd). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Ducks’ record (.500) is about what their chances are worth. The Kraken’s record (.553) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.430), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Ducks give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st) and have had shaky goaltending (30th). Anaheim has allowed 3.87 goals a game, the third most in the league. The Kraken rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (31st). They also give up a lot of shots (32nd), so the Ducks are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against them. Both teams like to play fast, especially the Ducks (4th), so expect an open game.

Cutter Gauthier (21 G / 8 A / 29 P in 22 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Leo Carlsson (6 G / 22 A / 28 P in 23 GP) is next in line. For the Kraken, Berkly Catton (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Brandon Montour (3 G / 11 A / 14 P in 18 GP) is next in line.

Anaheim has two options in net: Laurent Brossoit (4-1-0 / .866 SV% in 5 GS) and Lukáš Dostál (4-6-1 / .857 SV% in 12 GS). Brossoit has started five of their last ten games, but Dostál got the last one on Thursday. Seattle also has two options: Philipp Grubauer (6-4-1 / .897 SV% in 10 GS) and Joey Daccord (4-4-0 / .872 SV% in 9 GS). Grubauer has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday. For both teams, it’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
